clue.text: One excluded old theologian connected with a Mount, oddly

indicators.note: something done oddly is done strangely, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a Doctor of Divinity, the theology degree
the six letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric is shut out of a mountain community in some strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a hill or a horse, but with 'a' it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd man out is the single person left over or excluded from a group.

clue.text: Short operation on model's face

parts.note: OP is the usual shortening of operation
to model is to pose, as a sitter does for an artist

explanation.surface: A quick cosmetic procedure is carried out on a fashion model's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' reads as a noun, part of the model; it is the verb meaning to confront.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an opponent or a proposal is to stand against it, which is what opposing means.

clue.text: Fellow on essential Nativity play animal?

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
something key is essential

explanation.surface: A man takes the vital part of the animal in the school Nativity play.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary traditionally rides a donkey to Bethlehem, so a child often plays one in a Nativity; the question mark flags this example.

clue.text: Behave in a troublesome way at college after play

indicators.note: after places the university piece behind the drama piece in the answer

parts.note: to act is to play a part
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: A student misbehaves at university after a drama performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at college, and 'going down' when leaving, is an old Oxbridge usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is the idiom for misbehaving or causing trouble, as a child or a faulty machine does.

clue.text: Shoehorning hose away in an attitude of smug superiority

definitions.text: in an attitude of smug superiority

indicators.note: letters sent away from their places end up scattered in a new arrangement

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone cramming stockings out of sight with a shoehorn looks rather pleased with themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away' seems to say the hose is removed, but every letter of both words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pictures someone sitting above others on a tall mount, behaving arrogantly and haughtily.

clue.text: No one's about to chastise unstable Catholic king in play

indicators.note: unstable letters will not stay put, so they are rearranged

parts.note: these ten letters rearranged
C is the abbreviation for Catholic
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: An erratic Catholic monarch in a drama is ready to punish someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like part of 'No one's about to', but 'No one's about' is the definition and 'to' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a smugglers' idiom meaning nobody is watching, so it is safe to proceed unseen.

clue.text: Object from cracker daily found on hearth, oddly

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper

indicators.note: oddly here means taking the letters in the odd-numbered positions

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Christmas cracker's trinket turns up oddly lying on the fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled apart at the British festive table; it bangs and holds a joke, a toy and a tissue crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The folded tissue crown is the classic item found inside a Christmas cracker and worn at dinner.

clue.text: Swing he composed, with bit of ragtime thrown in?

definitions.text: Swing he composed, with bit of ragtime thrown in?

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh
something thrown in goes inside the rest

parts.note: these seven letters rearranged

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter, here its first

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A composer writes swing music with a touch of ragtime, describing Gershwin's style.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the man: George Gershwin mixed jazz, swing and ragtime into his compositions.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin, American composer of Rhapsody in Blue, drew on jazz and ragtime idioms throughout his work.

clue.text: One held captive round Mount after end of speech

indicators.note: after puts the round piece and the mounting piece behind the selected letter
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter
a round shape is the letter O
to mount a play is to stage it

explanation.surface: A prisoner is taken round a mountain once the speech has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a hill, but it is the verb used of putting on a production.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person seized and held captive as security for demands.

clue.text: Social worker after cloth, one with stripes

indicators.note: after places the worker piece behind the fabric piece in the answer

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric
ants are social insects and workers in a colony

explanation.surface: A social worker follows a piece of cloth, presumably a striped one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a caseworker; it is an insect that lives in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant wears three chevrons on the sleeve, the stripes that mark the rank.

clue.text: Personal assistant's to take home one Christmas cake

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation
take-home pay is pay after deductions, the nett amount
taken as written

explanation.surface: A secretary is going to carry a festive cake back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take home' sounds like carrying something; it is the pay left after tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Panettone is a tall Italian sweet bread with dried fruit, traditionally eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Rushes jobs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: speeds along out of control
second meaning: professions followed through working life

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words look like a headline about hasty hiring; they are separate meanings, one verb and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that careers hurtles wildly, and careers as a noun are lifelong occupations or professions.

clue.text: High, the Parisian church tower with spire

parts.note: steep means high, as of a cliff or a price
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A lofty Paris church has a tall tower topped with a spire.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall structure on a church, a tower usually crowned by a pointed spire.

clue.text: Saw ghost floating across rear of theatre in pantomime?

indicators.note: letters floating about drift free of their order
lying across something means spanning it, so the rearranged letters go either side

parts.note: these eight letters rearranged

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Someone saw a ghost drifting across the back of the theatre during a panto.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas theatre tradition of fairy-tale shows with comic dames and audience shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is one kind of theatrical production, so it is an example of the broader term, which the question mark signals.

clue.text: Ballet in middle of Christmas week, an excess

indicators.note: the middle of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter

parts.note: the central letter
W is the abbreviation for week
taken as written
a surplus of produce is called a lake, as in a wine lake

explanation.surface: A ballet is staged in the week of Christmas, amid seasonal overindulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: A wine or milk lake is EU jargon for a stored surplus, like a butter mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake is a famous ballet, often staged over the Christmas season.

clue.text: One involved in pantomime turn again?

definitions.text: One involved in pantomime turn again?

parts.words: One involved in pantomime turn again?
parts.note: surface reading: a performer who does another turn on the panto stage; setter's reading: the bells of London told the hero to turn again and he became Lord Mayor

explanation.walkthrough: In the legend, a poor lad leaving London hears Bow Bells chime 'Turn again'; he goes back and becomes Lord Mayor three times. His story is a favourite British Christmas pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: The panto hero, with his cat, is the one told by the bells to turn again, which is the clue's reference.

clue.text: Revulsion shown by DI, say, about latest of assaults

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means around, so the declaring word wraps the selected letter

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its last

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A detective inspector shows disgust at the most recent of a string of attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'DI, say' looks like 'a DI, for example', a detective inspector; DI is simply its own two letters and 'say' is the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is strong dislike or aversion, a milder form of revulsion and close synonym.

clue.text: Hears a CD prepared for Christmas party game?

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: these eight letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone listens to a CD readied for the festive party.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is the miming guessing game traditionally played at family gatherings over the holiday; the question mark admits it is not only for Christmas.

clue.text: Checks in chess? Aunt confused

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled into another order

parts.note: these nine letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A bewildered aunt asks what checks are in a game of chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' is the chess word the surface wants, but here it means stops a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch bleeding is to stop or check its flow, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Fixture in stable causing male irritation

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
anger is strong irritation

explanation.surface: Something fixed in a stable irritates a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' reads as steady, but it is the building where horses are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is the feeding trough fixed in a stable, famous as the infant Jesus's crib.

clue.text: Priest reportedly shot playing billiards

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is told, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a canon is a cathedral clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman was apparently shot while playing billiards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests a gunshot; it is a stroke at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a cannon is a stroke where the cue ball strikes both other balls in turn.

clue.text: Hypocrisy at a choral work

parts.note: cant is hypocritical pious talk
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the hypocrisy of a choral piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a composition for voices and instruments, such as Bach wrote for church services.

clue.text: Girl I lament over

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to moan is to lament

explanation.surface: A girl says she is grieving over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female given name, from the Book of Ruth, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: A soldier shown round small house of a native American

indicators.note: turned round means facing back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
a para is a paratrooper
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A soldier is given a tour of a little home belonging to a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like showing someone around the house; it turns back only the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains, so one of them fits.

clue.text: Instrument, unusual in one regard

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their ordinary order

parts.note: these nine letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: An instrument that is out of the ordinary in one respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ, such as a harmonium, is a keyboard instrument sounding through vibrating reeds rather than pipes.

clue.text: University stopping dissertations in ancient Greek

indicators.note: a stopper sits inside an opening, so one piece is plugged into the other

parts.note: theses are long academic dissertations
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university halts dissertations written in Ancient Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient Greek' reads as a language; it is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the hero of Greek myth who slew the Minotaur in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: Previously ending in Alsace, then Lorraine, strangely

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd fashion, so the letters fall in an odd order
the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter
taken as written, then rearranged with the letter before it

explanation.surface: Something formerly happened in Alsace and then, oddly, in neighbouring Lorraine.
explanation.walkthrough: Alsace and Lorraine are neighbouring French regions often named together.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier on means at a previous time, before now, which is the sense of previously.
